newsitem.title: MACAU: Jubilant Macau celebrates Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Jubilant Macau celebrates Hong Kong handover.

text.p: Thousands of mostly ethnic Chinese took to the streets of Macau during the night in a jubilant celebration of Hong Kong's return to China -- the destiny that awaits this Portuguese-run enclave in 1999.
Macau is the last bit of mainland China under foreign administration after Britain handed Hong Kong back at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.

In Macau's central Largo do Senado square thousands cheered as the clock struck midnight and television screens showed the historic sovereignty transfer taking place 60 km (40 miles) across the sea in Hong Kong.
Neighbourhood groups sympathetic towards Beijing staged dragon dances and sang patriotic songs, and community leaders gave speeches welcoming Hong Kong's "return to the motherland".
Speakers used the occasion to urge the Macau government to speed up the process of handing over to local Chinese key jobs occupied by Portuguese in the administration.
"We are all happy that Hong Kong is handed back to the motherland, and Macau will follow in 1999," said Maria Cheang, a 55-year old housewife and mother of five.

"I am very upset that the Macau government does not give us a public holiday on Tuesday. It's not fair because we are all Chinese, here in Macau, Hong Kong, Taiwan and on the mainland," said 27-year old office clerk Pedro Chung.
Tuesday and Wednesday are holidays in Hong Kong but normal working days in Macau, except for banks, which follow Hong Kong banking holidays.
Cheang and Chung were in the crowd on the square wearing yellow t-shirts handed out by neighbourhood groups.
Macau trade unions organised a patriotic "karaoke session" involving hundreds of workers at their soccer pitch near the famous Lisboa casino.
A "Hong Kong countdown clock" ticked away the last hours of British rule on the Largo do Senado.
The main casino company, controlled by tycoon Stanley Ho, staged a "Welcome Hong Kong's return to the motherland" fireworks display along the Praia Grande Bay waterfront at midnight.
Macau reverts to Chinese administration at midnight December 19/20 in 1999, after 442 years of Portugese rule.
Like Hong Kong, the 21 sq km territory of 455,000 residents will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.
The territory is no longer called a colony, but Chinese territory under Portugese administration. Lisbon has already conceded sovereignty to China.
Most Macau people, 95 per cent of whom are ethnic Chinese, watched the Hong Kong handover ceremonies on two Chinese-language television channels beamed from Hong Kong.
Macau's Governor, General Vasco Rocha Vieira, and Legislative Assembly President Anabela Ritchie, attended the handover ceremonies in Hong Kong.
